glossary.definition: Fine-tuning is taking an already-trained AI model and training it further on a smaller, specific dataset so it gets better at a particular task or domain, like legal writing, customer support, or a company's internal jargon. It's the AI equivalent of hiring a smart, broadly educated generalist and then sending them through a few weeks of specialized on-the-job training, instead of educating a brand new specialist from kindergarten onward. It's far cheaper and faster than training a model from scratch.

items.title: Microsoft’s email security is unexpectedly blocking legitimate business mail
items.summary: Microsoft’s email filters meant to protect users from malicious messages appear to be rejecting legitimate ones. Over the last few days, some mail sent to Microsoft consumer addresses have bounced if they did not publish a domain-based message authentication, reporting, and conformance (DMARC) record. This includes messages to Outlook, Hotmail, Live, and MSN. The refusals began November 5 and are ongoing as of publication time .

items.title: Meta introduces Muse Ember to power cost-efficient AI agents
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. today introduced Muse Ember, an entry-level artificial intelligence model that costs significantly less than the competition. Notably, it’s the first AI that the company trained using Muse Wonder. The latter algorithm is the Facebook parent’s flagship large language model. Meta didn’t specify which part of the workflow it automated with Muse Wonder.

items.title: Mphasis Raises FY27 Growth Outlook After 9.2% Dollar Revenue Growth in Q2
items.summary: Mphasis has raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to the low double-digit range after reporting 9.2% year-on-year growth in dollar revenue in Q2 FY27. The company had previously expected growth in the high single digits to low double digits. Revenue grew 3.2% sequentially to $486.1 million, while constant-currency growth stood at 3.3% QoQ and 9.7% YoY. In rupee terms, revenue increased 17.4% annually to ₹4,580.9 crore.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
items.summary: The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported. Launching a major tech IPO would seem risky right now, shortly after one of Nasdaq’s biggest sell-offs and amid revelations that a CEO central to the AI boom had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But that isn’t deterring Anthropic, which is moving ahead with its listing plans, according to The Wall Street Journal . Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, the Journal reported.

items.title: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
items.summary: During Paramount Skydance's latest earnings call , CEO David Ellison said "it's hard to imagine" AI won't have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company's outlook for AI, Ellison said: "I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history. The last time we saw anything close to this was really the, you know, advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 90s. Paramount Skydance’s CEO compared AI to CGI, but said it ‘will never be a replacement’ for artists.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
items.summary: With a big checkbook and sought-after chips, Nvidia’s CEO had his thumb on the world of AI. An extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy may put all of that at risk. No executive has pulled the strings in the artificial intelligence era quite like Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang . He parlayed the boom into incredible wealth, became a close confidant of President Donald Trump, and emerged as a prominent voice in US-China relations.

items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly engaged a PR firm with a history of handling high-profile sex scandals a year ago
items.summary: The PR firm was enlisted shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report described Alice Huang's business dealings with Jensen Huang, Wired reported. , a crisis communications firm known for handling sex scandals, at least a year before he publicly acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, Wired reported . Heller Inc. founder Risa Heller has advised prominent men through personal scandals and sexual misconduct accusations, according to a 2023 New York Magazine profile.

items.title: Meta’s Conductor deal puts enterprise AI coding workflows on deadline
items.summary: The social media giant’s acquisition leaves developers facing a cloud shutdown and highlights that enterprises need to protect AI coding workflows and plan vendor exits.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
items.summary: Anthropic is releasing Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, its most powerful models to date, in two versions: one freely available and one reserved for verified organizations. The models solve open physics problems, show stronger cybersecurity capabilities, design functioning operating systems, and write more than 90 percent of the changes merged into Anthropic's core code, according to the company. Anthropic says it has deliberately curbed any capabilities that would let the AI accelerate its own development. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 reclaim the AI performance lead shortly before the company's IPO, in some cases by a wide margin.

items.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
items.summary: As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.

items.title: SpaceX now fundamentally an "infrastructure company," senior official says
items.summary: For a long time, SpaceX has been synonymous with the development of newer, larger, and ever-more-reusable rockets. But that began to change over the last decade with the introduction of Starlink, and the change has accelerated during the last 18 months as the company has pivoted to data and artificial intelligence. Summit conference in Florida, the vice president of launch at SpaceX, Kiko Dontchev, offered some of the most revealing comments to date about the company's changing focus, how it is embracing AI, and why the Falcon 9 rocket—which has dominated global launch for a decade and remains the world's preeminent launch vehicle—is firmly on the road to retirement. "In the last couple years, when I talk about SpaceX, yes, we are a rocket company, but fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point," Dontchev said.

items.title: How neurosymbolic AI can transform enterprise decision-making
items.summary: Agentic AI has become a powerful enterprise business tool with increasing capabilities, and it has never been easier to address business pain points by applying a large language model (LLM) to develop a plausible automated solution. But is that solution as reliable as you need it to be, especially when the insights gleaned are used to inform critical business decisions? LLMs are incredible resources that play a significant role in a business’s agentic AI infrastructure. But when they have to work across complex data sets, business policies, industry regulations, decision hierarchies, and multiple software systems, they do not inherently provide the enterprise-grade provenance needed to show which evidence, assumptions, constraints, and decision logic produced a recommendation.
